Had these been FROZEN the rebase would have been forbidden and the move would have been SUPERSEDED and a fresh freeze.

The 2026-09-06 shape passes; a declared node containing the real one is refused; a declared node contained by the real one is refused; a live address with a contradictory node is refused; an address under another node's directory is refused; an address from an invented parent is refused; a missing address is refused; a citation of an earlier head whose address does not name that head is refused, and the same citation with the address that head names passes, which is the behaviour that keeps a superseded citation readable.

residual_not_held_against_the_change.R2_the_other_containment_direction: The mutant reading the real node as contained in the declared one - _node_id_of(_export_node(path)) in node - survives the shipped suite. It is killed by the case this witness handed over in pass 3, declaring node:local-2 against a node:local export, which was replaced by the node:loc case rather than joined to it. The two directions of one comparison want two lines in the same case. This is recorded as a residual and not as a condition, because the harm it admits is bounded: the address equality is still built from the real node's directory, so what would pass is a report whose node field names something that does not exist while its address is otherwise correct. Handing over the case and letting the concern absorb it is the right end for it.

observed.small_caution: Two of the repaired cases now assert on generic fragments - 'names /' or 'names nodes/' - where the earlier wording pinned a specific refusal. They do discriminate here, since three mutants die on them, but an assertion that broad pins the shape of a message rather than its meaning. Related and this witness's own: my pass-3 two-node case asserted a refusal string the repair reworded, so it failed against these bytes until I updated it. Cases coupled to message text age with the messages; that is worth knowing before the next rewording, not a defect in this change.
